independent_solution: Launch and landing on the floor, no drag, g = 9.8 m/s^2. Maximum height H = v0^2 sin^2(theta)/(2g); a 45 deg throw would reach 1600 x 0.5/19.6 = 40.8 m > 25 m, so the ceiling limits the angle.
R = v0^2 sin(2 theta)/g rises with theta below 45 deg, so the best throw just touches 25 m: sin(theta) = sqrt(2 x 9.8 x 25)/40 = 22.14/40 = 0.5534, theta = 33.6 deg.
The greatest range for a launch speed v0 is at 45 deg: v0^2/g = 100 m.
The greatest height for the same speed is a vertical throw: h = v0^2/(2g) = 100/2 = 50 m.
For a fixed v0 on level ground, R = v0^2 sin(2 theta)/g, so R is proportional to sin(2 theta).
R(45)/R(15) = sin(90 deg)/sin(30 deg) = 2, so R(45) = 100 m: option (c).
